newsitem.title: UK: T-bonds ease off in London, pre-FOMC nerves grow.
newsitem.headline: T-bonds ease off in London, pre-FOMC nerves grow.

text.p: Treasuries eased back in London on Monday as dealers reported extremely light activity ahead of Tuesday's U.S. monetary policy-setting meeting.

Players said the mood in the market was nervous, with opinion mixed on what the Federal Reserve Open Market Committee's decision will be on U.S. interest rates. "There is very little movement in the market this morning," said one trader at a U.S. bank in London.
"Everyone has either already put a bet on or is running square books, and there is a general feeling of "why do anything?'," he said. "Why take the risk?"
The benchmark 30-year U.S. long bond was quoted at 96-08 by 0847 GMT, giving a yield of 7.052 percent. The long bond was slightly lower than its 96-09 Tokyo and 96-10 New York bid closes.
In the futures market, December T-bond contracts were trading 2/32 lower at 107-22 in automated trade, while December eurodollars were at 94.06.
The spread of 10-year U.S. yields over Germany was trading at around 78 basis points by the same time.
In a poll of 30 economists surveyed last week, 17 said they expected the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy on Tuesday, with all but one of those 17 forecasting at 25 basis point rise.
The federal funds rate is currently 5.25 percent.
But analysts said with presidential elections approaching on November 5, the U.S. central bank was in a tricky position and market opinion was keenly divided on what it might do.
One London-based analyst, who thought a hike in rates was unlikely to materialise, said Treasuries were set for good gains if no move was made.
"If they don't hike there should be a decent rally at the short end and an initial rally at the long end," he said. "But overall I would expect the curve to steepen quite dramatically."
